ui.subtitle: Territory Command Terminal
ui.title: Recontinuation
ui.loginNote: Continuity Office. Authorized Commanders only. Progress Above All. Even now.

won.title: The Beacon is transmitting
won.text: The Series-9 Beacon has finished its message. Something out there heard it, Commander. The Office has no form for this.

failed.title: Colony written off
failed.text: Output fell below the cost of keeping the colony, and the Office has closed the file. The people have left, and Site 7 is empty.
failed.carry: The Office will carry {credits} Liquid Credits to your next assignment.

shutdown.title: Colony shut down
shutdown.text: Net Drag has run out, but the Office has not written Site 7 off. It has put the colony into shutdown: only the essentials are running, everything else is parked, and a skeleton workforce is holding on. Rebuild from here at your own pace.
shutdown.hint: If you would rather start over, Abandon colony is in the command menu.

ui.missionsHint: Earn a combined standing of 500 with the factions and your name will be known across the lands.
ui.requisitionsNote: The Office asks for ordinary goods, on a form, by a date. Deliver the full amount from the Core and it pays above the logistics run's price and lends the colony something for a while. A form that lapses is simply refiled.

solar_array.name: Heliostat Array
solar_array.desc: Salvaged solar panels, re-aimed by hand. The old grid is gone, so this is the grid. Nothing else here runs without it.

scrap_extractor.name: Reclaim Rig
scrap_extractor.desc: Strips the wreckage fields to the rivets. Feeds the assemblers.

water_pump.name: Aquifer Pump
water_pump.desc: Pulls toxic water from the aquifer. Undrinkable until filtered.

water_purifier.name: Cliffside Filtration Plant
water_purifier.desc: A filtration design from Cliffside Labs, the old medical and farming company. Turns aquifer draw into water a person can drink.

parts_assembler.name: LMAO Parts Press
parts_assembler.desc: Uses an LMAO printer (a matter printer that builds objects from molecular ink) to press reclaim into machined parts. The first real bottleneck.

hydroponics_bay.name: Nutrient Bay
hydroponics_bay.desc: Grows paste feedstock under lamps. Needs filtrate to run.

fabrication_works.name: LMAO Print Works
fabrication_works.desc: Runs the last working matter printers to make print stock for the largest structures. Hub upgrades need it.

scrap_generator.name: Reclaim Burner
scrap_generator.desc: Burns reclaim for serious power. The smoke shows from the next district. Wants a big plot to breathe.

synth_reclaimer.name: Ink Reclaimer
synth_reclaimer.desc: Turns surplus raw ink into polymers, two to one. The polymer plant makes more ink than the circuit line needs, and this puts the rest to work.

foundry.name: Black Foundry
foundry.desc: Smelts reclaim and parts into spine alloy, the strong structural metal Black Industries, the old mining company, once made for hulls and beams. Big furnaces need big plots.

circuit_fab.name: Phononic Fab
circuit_fab.desc: Prints circuitry that runs on sound waves instead of electricity, a FAILTECH design, from synthetics and polymers. Dust is the enemy. Needs the Gulf Stacks.

cell_forge.name: Klein Cell Forge
cell_forge.desc: Assembles Klein cells, compact fusion power packs, from alloys and circuits. Klein Energy would call it theft, but nobody is left to file. The most demanding build in the colony.

warehouse.name: Logistics Depot
warehouse.desc: Extra racking, tarps and padlocks. Raises the storage cap of every resource.

watch_post.name: Sentinel Post
watch_post.desc: Armed lookouts on the old Sentinel pattern, FAILTECH's watch-station network. Their combined strength decides how badly the Unaffiliated hurt you when they come.

beacon_array.name: Series-9 Beacon
beacon_array.desc: A rebuilt communication node of the kind FAILTECH once strung between stars. Set to speak, it can reach whatever is left of the world, if anything is. Only one can be built.

kitchen.name: Best Food Kitchen
kitchen.desc: Run under Best Food, the Office's ration label. Turns plain paste into heavy meals: real, cooked food. Hungry people survive on paste. People who eat well are happier and work harder.

dormitory.name: Class-C Dormitory
dormitory.desc: Communal bunks, the Office's lowest housing tier, for a few more colonists. Noise and fumes from neighbours make for poor sleep.

habitat.name: Class-B Habitat Block
habitat.desc: Private quarters, the Office's middle housing tier. Big, and worth placing carefully, because homes next to heavy industry are miserable.

ore_drill.name: Strata Drill
ore_drill.desc: Bores into the old strata for raw ore. Only the Black Cut has the seams.

smelter.name: Black Smelter
smelter.desc: Runs ore down into ingots. Wants a wide plot and a lot of heat.

alloy_works.name: Spine Alloy Works
alloy_works.desc: Bulk spine alloy from ingots: the heavy end of the Black Cut. Give it a Large plot and it outproduces the Core foundry.

crude_pump.name: Pipeline Tap
crude_pump.desc: Taps the old pipelines and tar seeps for crude oil.

cracking_tower.desc: Splits crude into fuel and the reagents everything else is hungry for.

polymer_plant.desc: Cooks crude into polymers, with raw ink as a by-product. The pipework needs ingots, and the Gulf Stacks make none.

fuel_generator.name: Fuel Turbine
fuel_generator.desc: Burns refined fuel for serious power.

bio_dome.name: Cliffside Bio Dome
bio_dome.desc: Sealed greenery under glass, watered straight from the valley springs. Grows biomass and makes the neighbours feel better.

agri_lab.name: Cliffside Agri Lab
agri_lab.desc: Cultures soil primer out of biomass and reagents.

pharma_lab.name: HTR Lab
pharma_lab.desc: Cooks HTR patches, the near-instant wound healers FAILTECH was famous for, from biomass, reagents and a little polymer packaging. Slow, and worth a lot.

trade_workshop.name: Licensed Workshop
trade_workshop.desc: FAILTECH licensed everything, and the habit survives. Turns colony goods into trade goods. Choose one recipe and it is locked in: changing it costs credits and idles the shop. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch (more in, more out), not a better one.

orbital_staging.name: Orbital Staging Platform
orbital_staging.desc: A gantry and fuel farm that assembles a payload for orbit. Load a launch cycle and it draws frames, fittings and modules every tick until the payload is complete, then waits for the catapult.

orbital_catapult.name: Orbital Catapult
orbital_catapult.desc: A mass driver that throws a finished payload into orbit. It must stand beside the staging platform, and it burns a little fuel just to stay warm.

orbital_command.name: Orbital Command Center
orbital_command.desc: The ground station for everything in orbit: tracking, telemetry and the people who read it. It must be running before anything can be launched.

klein_reactor.name: Klein Reactor
klein_reactor.desc: Burns power cells for the station grid. Nothing in orbit runs without it.

orbital_foundry.name: Orbital Foundry
orbital_foundry.desc: An automated workshop. Choose one recipe and it is locked in, like a trade workshop, but it needs no crew: it draws more power instead. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch.

t_tap.name: Anomaly Tap
t_tap.desc: Draws the territory's rare material out of the anomaly. Pick a recipe and it holds. What the material wants depends on what it is, and the first visits will teach that the slow way. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch.

t_data.name: Data Recovery Rig
t_data.desc: Works a data site. It needs only power. Each recovery attempt takes a long while and most find nothing, but the Office keeps asking, and the rig keeps answering. Low power slows it.

reclamation_plant.name: LMAO Reclaim Mill
reclamation_plant.desc: Takes Reclaim by the truckload and turns it into something the Office will count. What it makes depends on how the line is set.

cell_bank.name: Klein Reserve Bank
cell_bank.desc: Klein Cells on standby. When the Klein grid runs short it makes up the difference, and burns cells from this site's stock only for as long as it has to.

pits.name: The Black Cut
pits.desc: Strip mines and collapsed foundries of Black Industries, the old mining company, half swallowed by the Lapse. Ore comes out of the ground here, then ingots and bulk spine alloy.

stacks.name: The Gulf Stacks
stacks.desc: Flare towers and pipe-forests over the old Gulf Coast refineries. Crude, fuel, reagents and polymers, plus the raw ink and circuits built from them. Some towers still burn with nothing feeding them.

greenbelt.name: The Cliffside Reserve
greenbelt.desc: Sealed bio-domes in the one valley the anomalies spared, kept by Cliffside Labs, the old medical and farming company. Biomass, soil primer and HTR patches, if you can bring it what it lacks.

freeport.name: The Sanctuary Port
freeport.desc: A tax-free harbour on the far side of the wastes, from the years when corporations bought their own sovereign ports. Anything can be built here except the base-resource extractors of the other districts, and its workshops turn what you make into what anyone out there will pay for.

dust_storm.name: Ashfall Front
dust_storm.desc: A wall of ash and grit is rolling in off the dead ground. Solar output will collapse while it lasts.

equipment_fault.name: Phantom Drag
equipment_fault.desc: Machinery is wearing out faster than it should, for no reason any sensor can name. Several structures will lose efficiency until repaired.

blight.name: Chirality Blight
blight.desc: The growing beds are flipping to mirror-image chemistry. The crops look healthy and feed nobody. Food output will crash.

raid.name: Unaffiliated Raid
raid.desc: Survivors with no colony and no charter have spotted yours. Unguarded stockpiles will be looted and outer buildings damaged.

toxic_spill.name: Aquifer Bleed
toxic_spill.desc: Something is bleeding into the aquifer from below. Water extraction and filtration will crawl.

cold_snap.name: Thermal Wall
cold_snap.desc: The temperature is falling toward a limit nobody can explain. A killing cold is coming. The colony will burn through water and paste far faster.

signal_storm.name: Orpheus Cascade
signal_storm.desc: A harmonic feedback loop, named for an old FAILTECH drive accident, is building across the radio bands. The beacon will struggle to transmit.

cinder.name: Black Industries Remnant
cinder.desc: What is left of the foundry crews of Black Industries, the old mining and materials company. They pay well for anything that cuts or carries a load.

verdant.name: Cliffside Accord
verdant.desc: Cliffside Labs' surviving growers and wardens. Cliffside was the old medical and farming company. They want medicine, comfort and anything that keeps the green alive.

meridian.name: Ammano Transit
meridian.desc: Road-and-rail crews of Ammano, the old manufacturing and freight company, still moving cargo through the ruins. They buy finished goods by the crate.

crews.name: Seconded Work Crews
crews.desc: The Office lends hands. Work under way moves one extra cycle every third cycle.

convoy.name: Priority Run Slot
convoy.desc: The logistics run carries a quarter more of everything, for now.

water_purifier.scrap_bed.name: Reclaim-Bed Filtration
water_purifier.scrap_bed.desc: Runs the draw through beds of crushed Reclaim. More Filtrate from the same plant.

water_purifier.reagent_dose.name: Reagent Dosing
water_purifier.reagent_dose.desc: Doses the intake with Reagent Stock and runs the plant flat out.

hydroponics_bay.biomass_feed.name: Mycelial Feedstock
hydroponics_bay.biomass_feed.desc: Feeds the beds on Mycelial Biomass from the Reserve. Heavier crops under the same lamps.

parts_assembler.ingot_stamping.name: Ingot Stamping
parts_assembler.ingot_stamping.desc: Stamps parts from Ingots instead of sorting them out of Reclaim.

fabrication_works.polymer_bound.name: Polymer-Bound Stock
fabrication_works.polymer_bound.desc: Binds shredded Reclaim with Polymer Stock. Eats Reclaim, prints a great deal.

foundry.ingot_charge.name: Ingot Charge
foundry.ingot_charge.desc: Charges the furnace with Ingots and tops it up with Reclaim.

foundry.flux_refined.name: Flux-Refined Pour
foundry.flux_refined.desc: A reagent flux lets the furnace take far more Reclaim per pour.

kitchen.preserved_stores.name: Preserved Stores
kitchen.preserved_stores.desc: Stretches Nutrient Paste with preserved Mycelial Biomass.

scrap_generator.fuel_assisted.name: Fuel-Assisted Burn
scrap_generator.fuel_assisted.desc: A splash of Refined Fuel keeps a much bigger Reclaim fire going.

ore_drill.fuel_drill.name: Fuel-Driven Bore
ore_drill.fuel_drill.desc: Runs the bore on Refined Fuel as well as the grid.

smelter.fuel_fired.name: Fuel-Fired Smelting
smelter.fuel_fired.desc: Burns Refined Fuel under the charge for a hotter, faster melt.

alloy_works.reagent_quench.name: Reagent Quench
alloy_works.reagent_quench.desc: Quenches in Reagent Stock and folds Reclaim into the melt.

cracking_tower.fuel_cut.name: Fuel Cut
cracking_tower.fuel_cut.desc: Sets the tower to favour Refined Fuel.

cracking_tower.reagent_cut.name: Reagent Cut
cracking_tower.reagent_cut.desc: Sets the tower to favour Reagent Stock.

cracking_tower.catalytic.name: Catalytic Cracking
cracking_tower.catalytic.desc: An ingot catalyst gets more of both out of the Crude.

polymer_plant.scrap_fed.name: Reclaim-Fed Polymerisation
polymer_plant.scrap_fed.desc: Feeds shredded Reclaim in as filler.

synth_reclaimer.reagent_wash.name: Reagent Wash
synth_reclaimer.reagent_wash.desc: A reagent wash recovers more Polymer Stock from the same Raw Ink.

circuit_fab.alloy_traces.name: Spine-Alloy Traces
circuit_fab.alloy_traces.desc: Lays traces in Spine Alloy instead of machining them from parts.

cell_forge.reagent_electrolyte.name: Reagent Electrolyte
cell_forge.reagent_electrolyte.desc: A reagent electrolyte and Reclaim casings: two cells from the alloy and circuits of one.

cell_forge.polymer_cased.name: Polymer-Cased Cells
cell_forge.polymer_cased.desc: Polymer casings and a full reagent charge. The forge at its limit.

fuel_generator.afterburn.name: Reagent Afterburn
fuel_generator.afterburn.desc: Injects Reagent Stock into the exhaust for a second burn.

bio_dome.fertilised_beds.name: Primed Beds
bio_dome.fertilised_beds.desc: Feeds the dome its own Soil Primer.

agri_lab.reagent_fixed.name: Reagent-Fixed Primer
agri_lab.reagent_fixed.desc: Fixes the mix with Reagent Stock from the Stacks.

pharma_lab.polymer_capsule.name: Polymer Capsules
pharma_lab.polymer_capsule.desc: Polymer capsules keep more of every batch.

reclamation_plant.press_board.name: Pressed Stock
reclamation_plant.press_board.desc: Presses Reclaim and a few parts into Print Stock.

reclamation_plant.ink_leach.name: Ink Leach
reclamation_plant.ink_leach.desc: Leaches Raw Ink out of Reclaim with Reagent Stock.

reclamation_plant.frame_blanks.name: Frame Blanks
reclamation_plant.frame_blanks.desc: Turns Reclaim, Print Stock and a little Spine Alloy into Spine Frames.

reclamation_plant.fitting_blanks.name: Fitting Blanks
reclamation_plant.fitting_blanks.desc: Turns Reclaim, parts and a circuit into Dampener Fittings.

power.title: Power
power.hint: The hub's own supply will not carry much. Everything that wants energy competes for the same grid, and a shortfall slows all of it. This node recommends a source.

scrap.title: Reclaim
scrap.hint: Reclaim pays for every structure, and some machines consume it. The cache only ever goes down unless something is digging.

parts.title: Hard-Spec
parts.hint: The advanced structures need parts you are not holding. Nobody sells them cheaply, and they do not appear on their own.

water.title: Filtrate
water.hint: Water from the ground is poison. The colony drinks from clean tanks, and the tanks are draining.

food.title: Nutrient Paste
food.hint: Paste does not appear on its own. Growing it needs light, filtrate and components, and the beds take time to build.

adjacency.title: Good Neighbours
adjacency.hint: Placement matters. Inspect a structure to see who sits beside it, and consider who should not.

steady.title: Break-Even Certificate
steady.hint: Everything the colony consumes must be replaced. Watch the green and red rates beside your stockpiles and the grid at the top. Net Drag only pauses when the books balance.

market.title: The Logistics Run
market.hint: A run passes on a schedule, at prices that wobble with the road. It only carries what you arranged before it arrived, and it pays for surplus.

hub2.title: Room to Grow
hub2.hint: The first ring fills quickly. The Command Hub itself can be pushed further, at a price, and more of the map opens with it.

plots.title: Elbow Room
plots.hint: Some structures want more room than the inner rings offer. A cramped plot still works, at a cost. The outer rings are bigger.

housing.title: A Roof Overhead
housing.hint: The hub's own quarters only hold so many, and machines need people to run them. More homes mean more hands, and more hands mean more can run at once.

meals.title: Heavy Meals
meals.hint: Paste keeps people alive, not content. A proper meal does something paste never will, and it starts with the paste you already make.

quiet.title: A Quiet Corner
quiet.hint: People sleep badly beside furnaces and drills. Where the homes go decides how the neighbourhood feels, and a good meal can only offset so much.

storm.title: Weather Has Opinions
storm.hint: Something will eventually be headed your way. What the colony holds in reserve when it lands decides how badly it hurts.

materials.title: Print Stock
materials.hint: The larger upgrades want a feedstock nobody mines. Something has to print it, and that something wants a bigger plot.

hub3.title: Upkeep
hub3.hint: A bigger hub is a hungrier one. From here it draws on the colony just to stand, so plan for the drain before you pay for it.

alloys.title: Spine Alloy
alloys.hint: Structural metals need furnaces, and furnaces need room to breathe.

hub4.title: A Wider Circle
hub4.hint: Another ring, another bill. The upkeep climbs, and it now includes things you had to make.

district.title: Beyond the Walls
district.hint: The Command Hub is wide enough to reach past its own rings. Somewhere out there is ground worth holding, and it will have to be paid for from your own stockpile.

ore.title: Raw From the Ground
ore.hint: A territory makes its own power and keeps its own stockpile. Whatever it digs up has to be fed and powered before it is any use to the colony.

route.title: Standing Orders
route.hint: Hauling goods by hand does not scale. Some things are needed every cycle, and a standing arrangement can bring them without you. Mind how much the road can carry.

exchange.title: Name Your Price
exchange.hint: The Logistics Run takes what it is offered, at its own prices. Somewhere there is a board where you can say what you will pay, or what you will take, and wait for someone to agree.

synth.title: Something Synthetic
synth.hint: Plastics and fine chemistry come from the old refineries, a long way from the hub. Whoever works there will need metal they cannot make.

circuits.title: Fine Work
circuits.hint: Precision parts need ink, polymers, patience, and a plot that gives them space.

cells.title: Concentrated Power
cells.hint: Something has to combine your best alloys and your finest circuits into a compact power source. It is the most demanding thing you will build.

medicine.title: Something to Heal With
medicine.hint: The last materials for the transmitter are grown, not forged, in the one place that still has clean ground. It will want chemistry and polymers from elsewhere.

hub5.title: The Far Ring
hub5.hint: The outermost ring has plots big enough for anything. The Command Hub has to be strong enough to open it.

beacon.title: Form 7-B: Beacon
beacon.hint: A transmitter big enough to be heard across the ruins wants the largest plot, the finest materials and a great deal of power.

transmit.title: Hold the Signal
transmit.hint: It has to keep running, powered and supplied, until the message gets through. Anything that interrupts it costs you time.

harbour.title: Someone Heard
harbour.hint: The signal reached something. There is a harbour now that will take anything you can make, and it is not short of ways to waste your time. It will want paying for, in full.

mission.title: A Name on the Board
mission.hint: People there post what they need and name what they will pay. Doing someone a favour is a kind of currency, though nobody has said what it buys.

o_staging.title: Form 7-O: Staging
o_staging.hint: A payload has to be assembled before anything leaves the ground. The plans want the outermost ring of the Command Hub, and they are not cheap.

o_catapult.title: Form 7-O: Catapult
o_catapult.hint: A payload needs a push. Whatever pushes it has to stand right beside the platform that builds it.

o_command.title: Form 7-O: Command
o_command.hint: Nothing goes up without someone on the ground tracking it. The Sanctuary Port has room on its biggest plots.

o_cycle.title: Capital Investment
o_cycle.hint: The payload is built a little every cycle, for a long time, out of the harbour's best goods. Keep them coming until it is complete.

o_launch.title: Up
o_launch.hint: A finished payload is only cargo until it leaves. It will need a name that survives a radio.

o_reactor.title: Klein Grid, Orbital
o_reactor.hint: Nothing up there runs on sunlight or workforce. Something has to burn the colony's most concentrated power.

o_foundry.title: Automated Hands
o_foundry.hint: The station can make things, one recipe at a time, if it has the power to replace the people.

o_deploy.title: Down Again
o_deploy.hint: The anomalies have opened ground nobody has mapped, and it will not stay open. The station has a ship for that.

o_rare.title: Samples
o_rare.hint: What grows in an anomaly grows nowhere else. Getting it out takes a chain on the ground and a ship that leaves in time.

o_project.title: The Relay
o_project.hint: Every station on the relay is building the same thing, one project at a time. A dropship can carry your share.

drift.name: Slow Drift
drift.desc: The ground is moving, gently. It will close eventually.

bloom.name: Bloom
bloom.desc: Something is growing over the edges of the territory.

hush.name: Hush
hush.desc: Sound stops at the boundary. Nobody likes working here.

fold.name: Fold
fold.desc: Distances are wrong. The territory is folding shut.

shear.name: Shear
shear.desc: The anomaly grinds at anything parked inside it. Rich, and dangerous.

flare.name: Flare
flare.desc: A short, violent opening. The richest pickings, and the ship will feel every tick of it.

lull.name: Lull
lull.desc: Nothing happens here, slowly. The Office would call it a good place to learn. The material comes out of it reluctantly.

gloam.name: Gloam
gloam.desc: A long, dim opening. The ship's power runs thin and nobody minds the wait.

lattice_survey.name: Lattice Survey
lattice_survey.desc: Map the anomalies from orbit with a lattice of sensors.

seed_vault.name: Seed Vault
seed_vault.desc: A vault in orbit for every seed line that survived the Lapse.

deep_bore.name: Deep Bore
deep_bore.desc: Drive a shaft deep enough to find out what is under the anomalies.

quiet_array.name: Quiet Array
quiet_array.desc: Listen to the hum with something built to hear it.

relay_spire.name: Relay Spire
relay_spire.desc: A mast in orbit that every station can talk through.

commons.name: Mycelium Commons
commons.desc: A shared garden in orbit, grown from what the anomalies left behind.

gravity_well.name: Gravity Well
gravity_well.desc: Anchor the relay with a mass heavy enough to hold everything else in place.

p01.name: Charter Survey, Annex 0
p01.text:
Annex 0 is the survey that comes before the numbering. It was never filed. It was found clipped inside the cover of Annex 1, and Seven has since filed it as Annex 0 because there was nowhere else to put it.
Three surveyors walked the candidate ground in the first season: Pia Okonkwo-Reyes, Halvard Teague, and a junior with no recorded surname, listed only as "Ines, assisting". Each was told to mark the best site for the Command Hub and to say nothing to the others until the maps were compared.
The maps were compared on the third evening. All three marks fell within one pace of the same point. No instrument supported it. The ground there was neither the firmest nor the driest, and the sight lines were poor. What it had was this: it was the only place on the survey sheet where the three compasses, the three barometers and the one surviving theodolite agreed with one another.
Nobody argued. The minutes record the decision as "unanimous" and then, in a different pen, "unanimous, which is unusual".
Each surveyor privately believed the mark was already on the sheet before they began. A faint pencil cross sat at that point on the master map, in a hand Teague said was not his, Okonkwo-Reyes said was not hers, and Ines said was too neat to be anyone's.
The hub was built on the cross. The Office has no form for asking who drew it.

p02.name: Continuity Audit 4
p02.text:
Audit 4 examined the supply ledger of the seed depot for the quarter before assignment. The auditor's summary is one line: "No discrepancies." The Quartermaster has added a second line in the margin: "That is the discrepancy."
Every other ledger in the audit shows the usual wear. Spoilage, breakage, short deliveries, a pallet written off after a flood, a count corrected in a second hand. These are what a ledger looks like when people keep it. The depot ledger has none of them. Every line balances to the unit. Every delivery is entered on the day it arrived, in the same hand, in the same ink, with the same small flourish on the sevens.
It also does not stop. It is the only ledger the Office holds that records no break at all. The depot's roof is entered as collapsing "during the Lapse", yet the ledger carries on without remark, recording deliveries to a building that by the Office's own account had no roof, no door and no road.
The deliveries were small, regular and correct. They were of exactly the things a colony would need first: lamp oil, grain, thread, nails.
The Quartermaster signed the audit without comment. She then initialled the margin note, struck out the initials, and initialled it again.

p03.name: Relay Station Night Notes
p03.text: The relay station, on the night watch.
p03.text2:
Night notes, Maren Voss, relay technician. Final page of the log, inserted by hand.
The relay answers. It does not volunteer. I have tested this for as long as I have had the watch. Ask it the weather and it gives the weather.
Where I disagree with Seven is the reason. Seven says the relay is a counting device and that a counting device, once started, cannot be told to stop short of its target. I accept that. What Seven will not accept is that the target may be a number nobody has given me.
I have kept my own tally of what the roll reads. The first four names are the station roster. After that it reads the name of everyone the Office ever assigned to anything in this region. After that it reads names that are on no list I can find, and some that I now know are on the Founding Roll, which I was not permitted to see until the Commander arrived. After that it reads the whole thing again, in the same order, with one more name at the end.
My theory, for what it is worth, is that it is not counting us. It is counting what it was told to keep. I think someone told it to keep everyone, and nobody came back to tell it to stop.
A relay that only answers is waiting for a question. I have not found the one it was built for. If you are reading this at the station, ask it something. Something other than the weather.

p04.name: Site Report: The Slow Ground
p04.text:
Site report, territory survey. Compiled by Teodor Anders, field surveyor, for the Continuity Office.
Summary. The anomalies on the territory do not behave as weather, geology or fire. They behave as an arrival.
Opening. The ground does not crack. There is no dust, no sound and no debris. A seam appears and widens, and the soil at its edge does not look cut so much as thinned, the way a page looks where something has been rubbed out. The opening takes several minutes. The crews call it the slow ground, and the name is fair: nothing about it hurries.
Depth. Instruments lowered into a seam return zero for every reading, including the reading for the instrument itself. Anders's note: "I cannot say what is below. I can say that it does not object to being measured."
Objects. Things that fall in are not lost. The word the crews use is "put away". Three tools dropped by accident over the survey period were found in the stores the following morning, cleaned, oiled and shelved in the wrong place, which is the place the stores clerk would have put them.
Closing. A seam folds shut like a book. It closes over several minutes, from the edges inward, and it closes at the Office's shift changes. Not near them. On them. The hub bell sounds, and the ground begins to shut.
Hostility. I will not call it hostile. Hostile things do not wait for you to finish your tea.
Query to Continuity Node 7. I asked Seven why the shift changes were set at the times they were. Seven replied that the times were inherited with the Charter. I asked who inherited them, and from whom. Seven replied that it would file the question.
I have not seen the question filed. I have seen the ground close, on time, every day since.
p04.text2:
Addendum to the site report: tests, and what the crews made of them. Teodor Anders.
Test one. At the Commander's instruction the hub moved the shift change one hour later. On the first day the ground shut at the old hour, with no one on shift change, and reopened. On the second it shut at the new hour. On the third it shut at both, and then opened a little between them, as a guest might arrive at two parties and be seen at each. On the fourth day it went back to the old hour and has not moved since. We have no theory for the fourth day.
Test two. The bell was rung with the site empty. Nothing closed. The seam stayed open until a cook crossed it to reach the stores, and then it began to shut behind her.
Test three. A foundry crew from the Black Cut refused to cross at shift change. Their shift boss, Magdalena Valdivia, said the ground was waiting for them and that she did not like being waited on. It remained open for an hour and a half. It closed within a minute of the last person stepping across.
Returns. A boot I had placed at the seam's lip as a marker was gone in the morning. In its place lay a pair of gloves, dry and clean, labelled in an old Office hand with a name. I checked the name against the Founding Roll. It is entered there. It has a tick in the column marked Returned.
Three explanations were offered by the crews. Dr. Haddad believes the ground is tending, clearing space for what is to be sown. Valdivia believes it is a machine on someone's timer. Dispatcher Dimaculangan believes it is a queue: "You do not close the dock with freight still on the ramp."
I hold with none of them. I will record that all three are in the right handwriting for the Office, which is to say that they are explanations. The ground is not.

p05.name: Founding Roll
p05.text:
Archive note on the Founding Roll. Ansel Pell, archivist.
The Founding Roll is a single bound volume of 412 names, each on its own ruled line. It is printed, not written. The type is the Office's standard face from before the Lapse, the paper is the Office's standard stock, and the binding is stitched in a pattern I can match to nothing else in the archive except the Charter itself.
There are four columns: Name, Assigned, Arrived, Returned. These are ordinary columns. Every posting the Office ever made was recorded under the same four headings, and the last is the one used when someone comes home from field service. "Returned" is not a strange word in this building.
What is strange is the ticks. A great many names carry a tick in the Returned column. The ticks are in ink, in a steady hand, and they are dated. The earliest is dated before the Roll was printed. The latest are dated seasons ahead of today. Nobody on the Roll has yet been assigned anywhere from which they might return, and yet there they are, returned.
I looked at who was ticked. It is not the dead and it is not the living. It is not the old or the young. The only thing I can find in common is that the Office holds some record placing each ticked person somewhere else: a clerk posted to the Gulf who never left Colorado, a surveyor entered in two places on one day. One is a man whose death certificate I filed myself. His line has a tick, and in the margin, in pencil, the words "thank you".
The names are in no order I can name. I tried alphabet, rank, date of birth, region and height. The only pattern is at the top: the first four lines are the roster of Relay Station 3, a concrete hut at the foot of a mast. I have no explanation for why a roll of 412 should open with four people at a radio hut.
I should record that I do not believe the Roll is a list of founders. A founder is someone who found a thing. This is a list of people who have been counted, by someone who did not think that being counted was the same as being there.
p05.text2:
Archive note, continued. The foot of the Roll.
The last page of the Roll carries a signature block of thirteen ruled lines. Twelve are signed, in twelve hands, each with a title: Director, Deputy Director, Chief Archivist (my predecessor, long retired), and so on down to a clerk whose title is simply "Witness". The thirteenth line is ruled and headed "Commander, as assigned". It is unsigned.
On the Roll's own page the same line is blank in every column but one. Name, empty. Assigned, empty. Arrived, empty. Returned is ticked.
I put the page under the lamp. The signature line has an impression in it, as if a pen had pressed hard and left no ink. I raked the light across it and read the impression. It was a signature. It was not a name I know. I wrote it down and went to bed. In the morning I raked the light again and the impression read differently. I have now read it nine times. No two readings agree. The shapes are not unlike the signatures of people I work with, which does not include Seven, who does not sign.
I cannot say whose line this is. It is headed for the Commander, but the Commander has not signed it, and I will not ask the Commander to. I think the Roll is patient, and I do not know what it is waiting for. I am an archivist. I do not insert myself into a record. I note only that the line is already ticked, and that I was relieved to see my own name nowhere near it.
I have no theory. I have a worry. The Office's idea of a founder is someone it can rely on to come back, and the line is already ticked. I think the Roll does not doubt that you will.

p06.name: Archivist's Tray Log
p06.text2:
Tray log, selected entries. Ansel Pell, archivist. Cells are named by the place of the sample.
The Black Cut, ash. Warm to the touch on the day I took it. Warm to the touch today. It has been in the tray through the cold season. I have stopped putting it near the others.
The Cliffside Reserve, water. A thimble of it. It has not once moved when the tray was carried, though I took the stairs two at a time to test it. A surface that does not slop is a surface that has decided something.
The Gulf Stacks, glass. A chip from a flare tower lens. Held to the lamp it shows a room I do not recognise: a window, a table, a hand that is not mine reaching to turn a page. I have decided not to look at it again.
The hub, soil. Taken from the foot of the pencil cross, from beneath the first stone. This cell is the loudest. In the evening I can feel it through the desk.
On the chord. Each cell hums, but not the same note. When the lid is shut they sound together, and I believe the lid is not making the sound. I believe the lid is what allows us to hear a chord that was always being played. I have asked Seven to say whether this is plausible. Seven replied that it is a "tidy image". I do not take it as a compliment.
On the silence. For six days I left the tray open on the desk. It was quiet. For six days I was almost cheerful. On the seventh the ground opened at the shift change, exactly as it always does, and I went and shut the lid. I cannot claim a connection. I only record that I enjoyed the six days.
I have been asked by Seven not to compare the chord with the signal the beacon receives. I have complied. I have not been asked by The Signal, which asks nothing of anyone, and which has taken to sitting very still whenever I carry the tray past.
p06.text3: The tray, taken out to the beacon.

p07.name: The Lapse, As Filed
p07.text:
Form 9: Notice of Lapse in Continuity (Clerical). Filed by Continuity Node 7 on behalf of the Continuity Office. Transcribed here as filed, with the objections that were appended.
On the word. The Office chose "lapse" because it is a clerical word. A policy lapses. A subscription lapses. A membership lapses when it is not renewed. The Office wishes to be clear that nothing in this usage implies that anything was due.
1. Nature of the lapse. An interval during which the continuity of the record could not be confirmed. The Office has no evidence that anything other than the record was affected.
2. Period. Undetermined. Three clocks were consulted. Each gave a different beginning. The earliest beginning is later than the latest ending. The Office regards this as a formatting matter.
3. Last ordinary entry. The Colorado night log. The operator wrote a single word, "Quiet", and initialled it.
4. First entry after. A line in the same log, in the same hand, dated the day before "Quiet". It reads "Continued". The operator has not been located. The initials are the same.
5. Cause. Not stated. A cause is the business of the party responsible, and no such party has been identified. See section 8.
6. Surface conditions. Reported as "not as expected". Survivor accounts use the phrase "nine tenths destroyed", which the Office has been unable to verify and which may reflect the survivors' unfamiliarity with the surface.
7. Persons affected. Unknown. The Founding Roll is the Office's best count. It is not to be treated as a count of persons.
8. Remedy. The Office will re-establish continuity by founding colonies, keeping the record as it goes, and entering the lapse retrospectively as a clerical error. When the record is complete, the lapse will not have occurred.
9. Statements of survivors. Gathered by freight crews and entered without comment.
A herder: "The sky was the wrong shape for a while."
A ferry hand: "Nothing happened. We lost three days and found the town folded over like a letter."
A night nurse: "It was a silence. A very large silence, like a pause in a sentence that went on."
A teacher: "It was the Office. Everyone says so and nobody will say how."
A mechanic: "Somebody asked a question, and it was answered."
A woman at a well: "It was warm."
A man on the coast road: "I was there and I was also on the road. I have not worked out which of us came back."
10. Objections appended.
Quartermaster Hesper Vane: "The Office cannot enter an event as an error and then remedy it by building. One of those is a correction and the other is a farm."
Archivist Ansel Pell: "Section 5 refers to a party responsible. If there is none, then it is a lapse. If there is one, it has a name. I would like the name, or I would like the section to say there is none."
Continuity Node 7: "This node concurs with both objections. This node notes that concurring is unusual, and has filed a note to that effect."
11. Matters the Office considered and declined to enter. The Office received several observations in the first season which it was unable to classify and therefore did not classify. They are listed here so that it can be said they were listed.
That three persons in different places described the same silence in the same words, though none had met.
That the pencil cross on the master survey was already there when the survey was opened.
That a roll of the Office's staff, drawn up the week before, was found to be longer than the Office's staff.
That the night operator's initials appear on the sheet for a day on which, by the Office's own record, the night operator was elsewhere.
That every clock in the Colorado facility stopped, and that every clock in the Colorado facility continued to be correct.
That a ledger kept for the seed depot did not lapse.
The Office is satisfied that none of these observations bears on the cause. The Office is also satisfied that it does not know what the cause would look like.
12. Filed. Continuity is preserved. Nothing has been lost that cannot be re-entered.
p07.text3:
Charter for the Re-Establishment of Continuity, Draft One. Transcribed by Ansel Pell from the only surviving copy, with marginal notes in two hands. Struck text is shown in square brackets. The first hand wrote in green ink and the second in pencil.
Preamble. Whereas the record has lapsed, and whereas the Office is the keeper of the record, the Office establishes colonies in the territories left open, to hold the record until it can be resumed.
Article 1. Purpose. The purpose of each colony is to re-establish continuity.
Margin, green: From what?
Margin, pencil: From here.
Article 2. Authority. Each colony shall be held by a Territory Commander, who holds it in trust for the Office [until it can hold itself].
Margin, green: Which is it?
Margin, pencil: Both. In that order.
Article 3. The record. Each colony shall keep a record of every day. No day shall be omitted [even where none is lived].
Margin, green: Why strike it?
Margin, pencil: Because it is true.
Article 4. Enquiry. [The colony shall not enquire into the lapse further than filing permits.]
Margin, green: This should stay.
Margin, pencil: It should not. The answer will not file.
Article 5. The beacon. A beacon shall be raised. It shall carry no message but its own existence [and one question, to be agreed].
Margin, green: What question?
Margin, pencil: Agreed.
Archivist's note: No draft records the question.
Article 6. The hours. The colony shall keep its shift changes at the hours given in Schedule A, without alteration.
Margin, green: Why the hours?
Margin, pencil: It prefers them.
Archivist's note: Schedule A is not attached to any copy I can find.
Article 7. The port. A port shall be provided for trade with any party. The Office shall not enquire who keeps it.
Margin, green: Provided by whom?
Margin, pencil: Provided.
Article 8. Persons. All persons who have been counted shall be treated as present.
Margin, green: Even those who are not?
Margin, pencil: Especially.
Article 9. Date. This draft is dated the day before the founding of the Office.
Margin, green: Typographical.
Margin, pencil: No.
Article 10. Conduct towards the ground. The colony shall not close, fill, burn or seal any opening in the ground, nor cross it while it is open without need.
Margin, green: Is the ground a party to this?
Margin, pencil: It is the other party.
Archivist's note: I have shown this article to the field surveyor. He has asked that it be read to every new crew, and has asked that it not be read aloud near the ground.
Article 11. Visitors. Any party that arrives shall be received as the Office would wish to be received, and counted.
Margin, green: Counted as what?
Margin, pencil: As present.
Archivist's note: The relay at Station 3 reads the roll in a voice that would suit this article. I have not mentioned that to the technician.
Article 12. Ending. This Charter shall remain in force until the record is complete.
Margin, green: And when is that?
Margin, pencil: You will know. It will feel like being asked.
Archivist's note: I have read this margin eleven times. It is the only one I do not understand, and it is the only one I find comforting. I record both facts.
Signatures. Twelve lines signed. A thirteenth is ruled and headed "Commander, as assigned". It is unsigned.
Archivist's closing note. Draft Two does not exist. Draft One was ratified unchanged, margins and all, by an Office that does not appear to have noticed the margins. The green hand is that of the Deputy Director. I have compared it. The pencil I cannot identify, except that its capital letters match the pencil cross on the master survey in Annex 0. I draw no inference. I note only that of the two hands, the pencil is the one that is certain.

p08.name: Memorandum 0
p08.text:
To the Territory Commanders of the Continuity Office, and to whoever keeps their records after them. From the Director, with the concurrence of the Deputy, in what we are calling the final week of the Office as it was. Dated the final day. The final day has not been identified.
This is the last thing we will file. We have been asked many times what happened and we have been unable to answer. This memorandum will not answer it either. It will tell you what we considered, what we did, and what we ask.
What we considered. We held five explanations for longer than we should have. We set them down here so that you need not spend your first seasons rediscovering them.
One. A failure. Some system of ours, or of someone else's, failed in a way that exceeded its design. We have been unable to identify a system capable of that failure. We therefore conclude that no system of ours failed, which is the sort of conclusion a tired office reaches and a careful one does not trust.
Two. An act. Someone did this. No party has claimed responsibility, which is consistent with there being no party, and equally consistent with there being one.
Three. Weather. A natural event of great size. We note that a natural event cannot easily be dated both before and after itself.
Four. A reply. An earlier beacon of ours asked something, a long time ago, and was destroyed. It is possible that something heard. It is possible that a question can be answered at the wrong time, and that the answer is what we are living in. We do not claim this. We do not know how else to account for the word "silent" in the earlier record.
Five. Nothing. It is possible that nothing happened to the world, and that what lapsed was the means by which we are able to see it. The record is the only place in which the lapse is certain. A world that cannot be recorded cannot be said to have ended.
A sixth explanation has been added to the file in pencil, in a hand we do not recognise: "We are what lapsed." We have not struck it out. We have not been able to decide whether that is a failing of ours.
What we were not told. We were told nothing. We had been preparing for years, in the sense that we were in the habit of preparing. The depots were stocked before the lapse, in a quarter that an audit later found too tidy. We cannot explain how we knew to stock them. We prefer to say that we were cautious. We note that a cautious office would have stocked other things.
What we did. We seeded colonies in the places the ground left alone. We chose the sites by marking a map, and when the markings agreed with something we did not look further. Site 7 was chosen by a pencil cross we did not make. We built on it. In the Office's defence, nothing else agreed. We kept a roll of those we could count. We kept the hours. We raised a beacon, because the Charter says to, and because the alternative was to wait.
What we ask. Keep the roll. Keep the hours. Do not close the ground by force, because we are not sure it is ours to close. Build the beacon, and when it is built, listen as long as it takes. If something answers, do not hurry. If it asks, do not refuse without thinking, and do not agree without thinking either.
On you. We assigned a Commander to each site. We do not know why we assigned you. The Roll has a line for you. We did not write it.
We are sorry that this is all we have. We were an office, and we did what an office does. We filed. We hope that filing is not the whole of continuity. We have a suspicion that it is not, and the suspicion is the only part of this memorandum we are certain of.
If you are reading this, the Office has been right at least once, and it was about you.
Ilse Marrow, Director. Signed in three places. The signature differs in each.
Appended by Continuity Node 7: This node has verified the signatures. All three are the Director's. This node has no explanation. This node is attaching it anyway.
p08.text2:
The ledger of the colony's life. A ledger of the Office's pattern, ruled and headed in the Director's hand before the colony was founded. The entries were in place when it was opened.
Founded. A hub raised on a pencil cross. A bell hung. The ground closes at the bell.
The first harvest was brought in. The seed that was borrowed did better than the seed that was planted.
A second hand began keeping the roll. The first stopped.
Ore from the Black Cut, warm from the ground. Nobody asked why.
A port was lit on the far coast. The operator was not named. The trade was fair.
A beacon was raised, and powered, and left to hum.
A hum came back. It was not from the beacon. It was kept.
Someone present asked a question. The question was not recorded. It was understood.
The roll was read aloud, in full, and one name was added at the end. It was not a name the readers knew.
A traveller arrived who had not been expected. The traveller was fed, and counted, and left, and was counted again the following season.
The ground was crossed, once, at the wrong hour. It did not close. It waited. No one was hurt, and no one spoke of it afterwards.
A season passed in which nothing was recorded, and the entries are therefore the more careful.
A tray was opened for the last time. What was in it had gone quiet. What was in it had not gone.
The ledger continues for as many lines as the colony has seasons. The final entry is incomplete. It reads: "The colony was".
It does not finish.
Note from Continuity Node 7: This node did not make these entries. This node has checked them against the colony's record. Each of them, so far, is correct. This node has stopped checking. This node will not finish the sentence.
p08.text3: The last page, read at the hub.

foundry.name: Remnant Foundry Camp
foundry.desc: Black Industries hands around a furnace that went cold in the Lapse. It wants metal, hard-spec parts and fuel, and its builders work on your upgrades in return.

valley.name: Cliffside Homestead
valley.desc: Families on clean ground with nothing to plant it with. It wants filtrate, food and patches, and its people come to work your lines.

depot.name: Ammano Waystation
depot.desc: A junction with track and no rolling stock. It wants print stock, polymer and fuel, and carries your goods further in return.

hungry.name: Hungry
hungry.desc: It needs a quarter more of everything, and gives more back.

frugal.name: Frugal
frugal.desc: It gets by on less, and has less to give.

eager.name: Eager
eager.desc: Its people do much of the building themselves: every drive is a quarter smaller.

remote.name: Remote
remote.desc: A long way out. Drives cost more, and word of the help travels further.
